title: Short geodesics on the regular dodecahedron
statement: On a regular dodecahedron, unfold a geodesic beginning at a vertex $v$ through successive faces. Call it short if it ends at a vertex and meets no vertex in between, and call it type $A_0$ when the endpoint-angle parameters satisfy $\beta-\alpha=2\pi/5$. Prove that such a type-$A_0$ short geodesic beginning at $v$ never ends at a vertex at graph distance $2$ from $v$ in the dodecahedron's edge graph.

research_summary: Appears to remain open. The claim that no type-$A_0$ short geodesic from $v$ ends at a graph-distance-2 vertex is unresolved. Literature status: - This is a conjecture about periodic/short geodesics on the regular dodecahedron, part of Fuchs' broader program (related to his and Tabachnikov's work on billiards in the cube/dodecahedron; the dodecahedron's short geodesics were studied by Fuchs—Tabachnikov "More on periodic billiard trajectories in the cube" and the dodecahedron case). - Presented as open in Fuchs' 2020 paper; no later resolution of this specific $A_0$-not-at-graph-distance-2 claim was located via web search through 2026.
